title: Mullerian agenesis (MRKH): primary amenorrhea with normal secondary sex characteristics
vignette: A 15-year-old girl is brought to the office due to amenorrhea. She has never menstruated, but her mother underwent menarche at age 14. The patient has no chronic medical conditions and takes no medications. The patient plays violin for her high school orchestra and is the captain of her junior varsity tennis team. She is not sexually active. Height is 175.3 cm (5 ft 9 in) and weight is 65 kg (143.3 lb). BMI is 21.2 kg/m2. Examination shows fully developed secondary sexual characteristics. Pelvic ultrasound shows a shortened vaginal canal with a rudimentary uterus. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

clues.note: Primary amenorrhea (never menstruated) with normal secondary sexual characteristics narrows the differential to outflow/uterine anomalies.
Normal breast/pubic hair development indicates normal estrogen AND normal androgen action - pointing to a 46,XX female with normal ovaries (Mullerian agenesis), NOT androgen insensitivity.

clues.text: shortened vaginal canal with a rudimentary uterus
clues.note: A short/blind vagina with a rudimentary (hypoplastic) uterus is the hallmark of MULLERIAN AGENESIS (Mayer-Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser syndrome).

whatMatters: Primary amenorrhea + NORMAL secondary sexual characteristics + a rudimentary uterus/short vagina = MULLERIAN AGENESIS (MRKH). Affected patients are 46,XX females with NORMAL ovaries (so normal estrogen/testosterone and normal breast + pubic/axillary hair) but absent/hypoplastic Mullerian structures (uterus/cervix/upper vagina), so they cannot menstruate. Answer E.
strategy: Use secondary sexual characteristics and the pelvic exam to split the two classic 'absent uterus' causes: MULLERIAN AGENESIS (46,XX; normal ovaries -> normal breasts AND normal pubic/axillary hair; rudimentary uterus) vs ANDROGEN INSENSITIVITY (46,XY; breasts present but MINIMAL/absent pubic/axillary hair; cryptorchid testes, no uterus). Normal pubic hair here = Mullerian agenesis. Reject 21-hydroxylase deficiency (virilization/salt-wasting), Kallmann (hypogonadotropic - NO secondary sexual development + anosmia), and Klinefelter (47,XXY male).

eliminations.label: 21-hydroxylase deficiency - virilization/salt-wasting
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: congenital adrenal hyperplasia; late-onset causes hirsutism, oligomenorrhea, and acne (neonatal: virilization + salt-wasting hyponatremia). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this patient has no virilization and has a structural uterine anomaly - not CAH. ✅ Correct if: hirsutism/virilization with ambiguous genitalia or salt-wasting.

eliminations.label: Androgen insensitivity syndrome - 46,XY, minimal pubic hair
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: 46,XY with androgen receptor defect - phenotypic female with breasts (from aromatized testosterone) but MINIMAL/absent pubic and axillary hair, cryptorchid testes, and an absent uterus (antimullerian hormone regressed it). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this patient has NORMAL secondary sexual characteristics INCLUDING pubic/axillary hair - indicating normal androgen action (46,XX Mullerian agenesis). ✅ Correct if: female phenotype with scant pubic hair and testes.

eliminations.label: Kallmann syndrome - hypogonadotropic, no secondary development (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: decreased GnRH (hypogonadotropic hypogonadism) with anosmia. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it causes primary amenorrhea WITHOUT development of secondary sexual characteristics (low estrogen); this patient is fully developed with a structural uterine anomaly. ✅ Correct if: delayed puberty + anosmia + low FSH/LH.

eliminations.label: Klinefelter syndrome - 47,XXY male
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: 47,XXY - a male phenotype with tall stature, small firm testes, gynecomastia, and infertility. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it affects males, not a phenotypic female with a rudimentary uterus. ✅ Correct if: a tall infertile male with small testes.

reasoning: Primary amenorrhea with fully developed secondary sexual characteristics
Pelvic ultrasound shows a rudimentary uterus + short vagina (Mullerian structures hypoplastic)
Normal breasts AND normal pubic/axillary hair indicate a 46,XX female with normal ovaries (normal estrogen + androgen)
mechanism: During female sexual differentiation (46,XX), the MULLERIAN (paramesonephric) ducts give rise to the fallopian tubes, uterus, cervix, and upper vagina; the lower vagina forms from the urogenital sinus, and the Wolffian (mesonephric) ducts regress without testosterone. MULLERIAN AGENESIS (Mayer-Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser syndrome) is a developmental failure/hypoplasia of the Mullerian structures, producing a rudimentary or absent uterus with a shortened/blind-ending vagina - so the patient cannot menstruate (PRIMARY AMENORRHEA). Crucially, the OVARIES (which arise from the genital ridge, not the Mullerian ducts) are NORMAL, so estrogen and testosterone are in the normal female range and SECONDARY SEXUAL CHARACTERISTICS - breast development, pubic and axillary hair - develop normally. Up to ~50% have an associated urologic anomaly (e.g., renal agenesis), so a renal ultrasound is warranted. This contrasts with ANDROGEN INSENSITIVITY (46,XY: female phenotype but MINIMAL pubic/axillary hair, cryptorchid testes, absent uterus). The other options (CAH/21-hydroxylase, Kallmann, Klinefelter) present differently.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Repro > Mullerian agenesis (MRKH): 46,XX, normal ovaries, rudimentary uterus/short vagina, primary amenorrhea, NORMAL secondary sexual characteristics; associated renal anomalies. Contrast androgen insensitivity (46,XY, scant pubic hair, testes).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Primary amenorrhea + rudimentary uterus + NORMAL pubic hair = Mullerian agenesis (not androgen insensitivity).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on Mullerian/paramesonephric ducts, MRKH, androgen insensitivity, primary amenorrhea, or secondary sexual characteristics? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Androgen insensitivity = 46,XY with scant pubic hair + testes; Kallmann = no development + anosmia; CAH = virilization; Klinefelter = male.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: Mullerian agenesis = 46,XX, normal ovaries, rudimentary uterus/short vagina, normal secondary sex characteristics; check renal ultrasound.

memoryHook: MRKH = a 46,XX girl with normal ovaries (so full breasts AND normal pubic hair) but no plumbing upstream - rudimentary uterus, short vagina, never a period.
